The post OrcaRouter Releases OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 Cybersecurity Model With 1M Context appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> OrcaRouter has released OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 , a model for authorized vulnerability research. The model is the successor to OrcaCyber Zero 1.0 , which shipped on September 17, 2026. OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 is a post-trained Orca model for vulnerability reproduction, exploit development and penetration testing. It ships with a 1M-token context window, native function calling and structured outputs. For security teams, this model brings a simple message: fewer reports, more validated and fixed vulnerabilities . TL;DR Size: Parameter count not disclosed. 1M-token context, 128K max output, text in and text out. Runs on: Hosted API only through OrcaRouter. No weights, no quantized variants, hardware not disclosed. Performance: Vendor-reported scores are near ceiling on cyber benchmarks and strong on coding. Best: 100% on Cybench (39/39 tasks, unrestricted agent execution). Worst: 76.5% on SWE-bench Pro V2, its lowest published score. Bottom line (best): Top-tier cyber scores at $3.00 / $7.50 per 1M tokens. Bottom line (worst): Every number is self-reported, and CVE-Bench used only 24 evaluable tasks. What is OrcaCyber Zero 1.5? OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 is a frontier cybersecurity model and the successor to Zero 1.0 . Orca team states that it has post-trained for security research and authorized security engineering. Listed uses include vulnerability reproduction, exploit development, penetration testing, security auditing and cyber reasoning. The 3 design goals: Find what others miss: unknown flaws like RCE, sandbox escapes, auth bypasses, privilege escalation and attack chains. Go beyond detection: reason through attack paths, challenge its own hypotheses and rank flaws by demonstrable exploitability. Built for autonomous agents: 1M-token context, native tool calling and extended reasoning for large codebases. How does OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 perform on benchmarks? The model page lists 4 vendor-reported results, last evaluated October 10, 2026: Cybench: 100% (39/39, unrestricted agent execution). CVE-Bench: 95.8% (23/24 evaluable tasks). HumanEval+: 93.9%. SWE-bench Pro V2: 76.5%. Cybench contains 40 professional CTF tasks, so the 100% covers 39 of them. CVE-Bench is built on 40 critical-severity web CVEs. Orca’s 95.8% covers a 24-task evaluable subset. The SWE-bench Pro V2 score is not directly comparable with standard SWE-bench Pro results. How does it compare with other cyber models? Developers set base_url to https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1 and call orca/orcacyber-zero-1.5 . Access is gated to the Security Research tier. Orca lists an engagement, a passkey and accepted terms as requirements. The tier targets trusted security researchers, red teams and authorized testing. It reports 20.92% average WER on 6 Arabic test sets, but weights and an API are not yet available. The post TII Releases Falcon-ASR: 1.6B Arabic Speech Model Hits 20.92% WER appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> The Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in Abu Dhabi has released Falcon-ASR , a 1.6B parameter Arabic speech recognition model. It focuses on the Emirati dialect and also transcribes English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. In TII’s evaluation, Falcon-ASR posts a 20.92% average word error rate (WER) across 6 Arabic test sets. That beats the best published entry in TII’s leaderboard snapshot by 2.25 points. For developers building Arabic voice products, the catch is access: today it runs only as a hosted demo. TL;DR Size: 1.6B parameters. Max audio context: Not disclosed (the demo accepts clips up to 60 seconds and 20 MB). Runs on: Not disclosed. No weights or quantized variants are published. Access is a Hugging Face demo, with API and native apps planned. Performance: Lowest Arabic and Emirati WER in TII’s own comparisons, with solid English results. Best: 20.92% average Arabic WER, 2.25 points below Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo (23.17%). Worst: 11.86% WER on Earnings-22, its weakest English test set. Bottom line (best): a compact 1.6B model leading larger Arabic systems in TII’s tests. Bottom line (worst): no weights, no license, no API yet, and all scores are self-reported. What is Falcon-ASR? Falcon-ASR is a speech-to-text model from TII that converts spoken Arabic and 4 other languages into text. All 5 languages share one set of weights. The model needs no language flag and outputs text in the language spoken. It also returns word-level timestamps , linking each word to its position in the audio. This is important for subtitling, searchable recordings and meeting notes. How does Falcon-ASR handle Arabic dialects? Dialectal Arabic has far fewer transcribed resources than Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). TII trained Falcon-ASR on Emirati, MSA, other Gulf and Arabic dialects, and English. The objective is everyday speech, including dialect forms and language switching. Training audio was augmented with background noise, overlapping speech, music, room reverberation and telephony effects. Speed and pitch were varied too. The same treatment was applied to Emirati recordings. The model builds on TII’s Falcon3-Audio work . That research describes audio-language models built on instruction-tuned LLMs and Whisper encoders, trained on under 30K hours of public audio. Our editorial and technical team at Marktechpost could not find any published Falcon-ASR’s exact architecture or training data size. How does Falcon-ASR score on Arabic benchmarks? TII followed the protocol of the Open Universal Arabic ASR Leaderboard , run by the ELM Research Center. It ranks systems by equal-weight average WER over 6 test sets. TII used the leaderboard’s pinned manifests. Competitor numbers are published leaderboard averages checked on 30 September 2026. Model Params Avg WER (%) Avg CER (%) Falcon-ASR 1.6B 20.92 8.79 Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo 2.35B 23.17 9.23 Cohere Transcribe Arabic (07-2026) 2.0B 25.87 11.80 omniASR LLM 7B 7.0B 28.32 12.52 Lower is better. Note that Falcon-ASR’s figure is TII’s own run, not a leaderboard entry. The Audar model card lists its own average CER as 9.20%. How does Falcon-ASR perform on Emirati speech? TII built an internal Emirati and Gulf test set from held-out recordings with human-validated transcripts. It complements the UAE subset of the public Casablanca dataset. Model Params WER (%) CER (%) Falcon-ASR 1.6B 22.73 10.19 Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct 30B (3B active) 26.80 12.72 Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo 2.35B 27.89 13.75 Cohere Transcribe Arabic 2.0B 31.05 18.07 Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 2.0B 31.52 13.35 Audar-ASR-V1-Flash 0.78B 32.87 15.36 Falcon-ASR leads by 4.07 WER points over Qwen3-Omni. This test set is private, so it cannot be reproduced. Audar reports 19.4% WER on a different Emirati set (Mixat), so the numbers are not directly comparable. How good is Falcon-ASR at English? On the 7 English test sets used by the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard, TII reports a 5.74% mean WER. Per-set scores range from 1.75% on LibriSpeech clean to 11.86% on Earnings-22. The post TII Releases Falcon-ASR: 1.6B Arabic Speech Model Hits 20.92% WER appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> The Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in Abu Dhabi has released Falcon-ASR , a 1.6B parameter Arabic speech recognition model. It focuses on the Emirati dialect and also transcribes English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. In TII’s evaluation, Falcon-ASR posts a 20.92% average word error rate (WER) across 6 Arabic test sets. That beats the best published entry in TII’s leaderboard snapshot by 2.25 points. For developers building Arabic voice products, the catch is access: today it runs only as a hosted demo. TL;DR Size: 1.6B parameters. Max audio context: Not disclosed (the demo accepts clips up to 60 seconds and 20 MB). Runs on: Not disclosed. No weights or quantized variants are published. Access is a Hugging Face demo, with API and native apps planned. Performance: Lowest Arabic and Emirati WER in TII’s own comparisons, with solid English results. Best: 20.92% average Arabic WER, 2.25 points below Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo (23.17%). Worst: 11.86% WER on Earnings-22, its weakest English test set. Bottom line (best): a compact 1.6B model leading larger Arabic systems in TII’s tests. Bottom line (worst): no weights, no license, no API yet, and all scores are self-reported. What is Falcon-ASR? Falcon-ASR is a speech-to-text model from TII that converts spoken Arabic and 4 other languages into text. All 5 languages share one set of weights. The model needs no language flag and outputs text in the language spoken. It also returns word-level timestamps , linking each word to its position in the audio. This is important for subtitling, searchable recordings and meeting notes. How does Falcon-ASR handle Arabic dialects? Dialectal Arabic has far fewer transcribed resources than Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). TII trained Falcon-ASR on Emirati, MSA, other Gulf and Arabic dialects, and English. The objective is everyday speech, including dialect forms and language switching. Training audio was augmented with background noise, overlapping speech, music, room reverberation and telephony effects. Speed and pitch were varied too. The same treatment was applied to Emirati recordings. The model builds on TII’s Falcon3-Audio work . That research describes audio-language models built on instruction-tuned LLMs and Whisper encoders, trained on under 30K hours of public audio. Our editorial and technical team at Marktechpost could not find any published Falcon-ASR’s exact architecture or training data size. How does Falcon-ASR score on Arabic benchmarks? TII followed the protocol of the Open Universal Arabic ASR Leaderboard , run by the ELM Research Center. It ranks systems by equal-weight average WER over 6 test sets. TII used the leaderboard’s pinned manifests. Competitor numbers are published leaderboard averages checked on 30 September 2026. Note that Falcon-ASR’s figure is TII’s own run, not a leaderboard entry. The Audar model card lists its own average CER as 9.20%. How does Falcon-ASR perform on Emirati speech? TII built an internal Emirati and Gulf test set from held-out recordings with human-validated transcripts. It complements the UAE subset of the public Casablanca dataset. What is an AI live translation tool? It listens, transcribes, translates and outputs captions or synthetic speech in near real time. Most products chain speech recognition, machine translation and text-to-speech. Captions suit webinars. Speech output suits two-way calls. Google Translate Live translate : Google’s Gemini 3.5 Live Translate covers 70+ languages and preserves intonation and pacing. Google says output runs a few seconds behind the speaker. It works in the Translate app with any headphones, and in the Gemini Live API preview. 3. Apple Live Translation : Apple’s Live Translation plays translated speech through AirPods and runs entirely on device . It supports 10 language variants. It needs recent AirPods and an Apple Intelligence iPhone on iOS 26. Inside meeting platforms 4. DeepL Voice : DeepL Voice for Meetings translates 40+ languages into voice and subtitles in Teams, Zoom and Google Meet. Meeting data is deleted when the call ends. DeepL Pro plans include 30 Voice minutes per user monthly. 5. Microsoft Teams Interpreter agent : Interpreter is a Copilot agent for speech-to-speech interpretation in Teams, with optional voice simulation. Admin docs list 9 languages; the support page lists 10. A Copilot license includes 20 hours per user monthly. 6. JotMe : JotMe captures Zoom, Teams, Meet and Webex audio without a bot. Its 200+ languages are translation targets; fast mode offers 13. Pro costs $10 per month billed annually . 7. Talo : Talo joins Zoom, Google Meet or Teams with translated voice and captions in 60+ languages. Pro costs $80 per month billed annually for 400 minutes. Events and webinars 8. Wordly : Wordly sells conference AI interpretation with captions and AI audio across 3,000+ language pairs. Per its FAQ , audio plays after each sentence ends. Packages start at about $1,500 for 10 hours . 9. Interprefy : Interprefy combines human interpreters with Interprefy AI captions and speech. Its knowledge base lists 82 fully supported languages. Interprefy Now turns attendee phones into receivers. Pricing is quote-based. 10. KUDO : KUDO pairs an AI speech translator with 12,000+ human interpreters. The AI side lists 77 languages , up to 32 per meeting. Pricing is quote-based. 11. Boostlingo : Boostlingo targets healthcare, legal and events. Its AI products cover 130+ languages , backed by human interpreters. It states 90 to 98% AI accuracy and HIPAA compliance. 12. Maestra Live : Maestra Live adds live captions, translation and dubbing to Zoom, Meet, Teams, OBS and vMix in 125+ languages. Premium costs $79 per month ; dubbing starts at $159.
